questions.question_text:
The cost per person $C$ dollars of hiring a hall is modelled by $C=\frac{900}{n}$, where $n$ is the number of people sharing the cost.
What does the $900$ represent?

options.text: The total cost of hiring the hall
The cost paid by each person
options.why: The cost per person is $C$, which changes with $n$; $900$ is fixed.

options.text: The number of people the hall can hold
options.why: Reads a dollar amount as a number of people.

options.text: The cost when $900$ people share the hire
options.why: With $900$ people sharing, the cost per person is $\$1$, not $\$900$.

questions.solution_text:
Rearranging gives $Cn=900$.
The cost per person multiplied by the number of people is the whole bill.
The $900$ is the total cost of hiring the hall, $\$900$.

questions.question_text:
The average speed $s$ km/h needed to cover $500$ km in $t$ hours is modelled by $s=\frac{500}{t}$.
Why does the graph never meet the horizontal axis?

options.text: $s=0$ would mean covering $500$ km at no speed, which no value of $t$ allows
The graph stops once $t$ reaches $500$
options.why: The curve continues for every $t$ greater than zero; it simply gets lower and lower.

options.text: Because $t$ cannot be negative
options.why: True in the context, but that is about the left of the graph, not about the curve meeting the horizontal axis.

options.text: Because $500$ divided by a large enough number eventually gives exactly $0$
options.why: Dividing $500$ by a larger and larger number gives smaller and smaller values, never exactly zero.

questions.solution_text:
A point on the horizontal axis has $s=0$.
That would need $0=\frac{500}{t}$, and no value of $t$ makes that true.
The curve gets closer and closer to the axis but never reaches it.

questions.question_text:
The cost per person $C$ dollars of a party is modelled by $C=\frac{600}{n}$, where $n$ is the number of guests.
Why can the model not be used for $n=7.5$?

options.text: The number of guests must be a whole number
$600$ is not divisible by $7.5$
options.why: It is: $\frac{600}{7.5}=80$. The problem is with what $n$ counts, not with the arithmetic.

options.text: The curve is not drawn that far along
options.why: How far a curve is drawn is a choice of window; it is not a limitation of the model.

options.text: The cost per person cannot be more than $\$80$
options.why: Fewer guests give a larger cost per person, so costs above $\$80$ are perfectly possible.

questions.solution_text:
The variable $n$ counts guests, and there cannot be half a guest.
The curve is drawn as a smooth line, but only the points with whole number values of $n$ describe a real party.
The model cannot be used for $n=7.5$.

questions.question_text:
The time $t$ hours to paint a house varies inversely with the number of painters $n$.
Six painters take $10$ hours.
What is the constant $k$ in $t=\frac{k}{n}$, and what does it mean?

options.text: $k=60$, the number of painter-hours the whole job takes
$k=10$, the number of hours each painter works
options.why: Uses the given time as the constant; the constant must be the product $6\times10$, not one of the two values.

options.text: $k=16$, the total of the painters and the hours
options.why: Adds the two values instead of multiplying them.

options.text: $k=\frac{5}{3}$, the hours per painter
options.why: Divides $10$ by $6$; the constant of an inverse variation is the product, not the quotient.

questions.solution_text:
$k=6\times10$
$=60$
Six painters each working $10$ hours is $60$ hours of painting in total.
The constant $60$ is the number of painter-hours the whole job takes.
